description: Visual search on Project AirSim Blocks: the policy gets Front/Down RGB and one sentence. Target coordinates are used only to place the vehicle, to drive the teacher and to score.

instructions.search_approach_land: Search for {noun}, approach it, and land.

B.label: visible, at the edge of the front view

D.label: seen, then lost after a forced turn

L.label: both objects in view from a place no training episode started at; the sentence names one

generalization.description: Start states and teacher for the generalisation dataset and its held-out tests (docs/aerovla_oft_generalization.md). Maps are in configs/maps/.

long_range.description: Fresh held-out starts by start distance (configs/long_range_test_spawns.json), planned after Gen-v2 was trained. No training episode starts farther than 70 m.

targeted_v2.description: Episodes added for Gen-v2: what to do once the target is found. Counts are [train, val]; `base` is the kind whose planning rules apply.

gen_v3.description: Gen-v3: precise grounding among distractors, far and small targets, and landing (docs/aerovla_oft_gen_v3.md). Kinds with a count are recorded as training data, [train, val]; the others are used by the fresh test set only. `base` is the kind whose planning rules apply; `task` is what the sentence asks for at the end.

round_b.description: Second round of additions, planned after the first Gen-v3 checkpoint did not pass the smoke gate (docs/aerovla_oft_gen_v3.md). Three of its four failed flights ended at an object of the right colour and the wrong shape; in the first round another object of the target's colour was nearer than the target in 5 of 240 starts. These kinds put that case in front of the model: the same pose told to go to each of several objects that share a colour or a shape, and starts where an object of the target's colour is nearer or is what the first view shows.

gates.description: Checks that must pass, in this order, before the 156 fresh test starts are flown (scripts/gate_gen_v3.py). Smoke and representative use validation starts of the training plan, never the test set. Fixed before the checkpoints they judge existed.

pilot.what: checkpoint trained on the pilot episodes alone, flown from 4 of their poses with both sentences

smoke.what: final checkpoint, the first validation start of each kind listed

representative.what: final checkpoint, every validation start the teacher finished

canonical.description: The canonical clean mission for the failure-aware experiments (docs/canonical_clean_baseline.md): find the blue landing pad and land on it, from at most 44 m. Farther starts are kept as a separate long-range challenge. No model is trained for this; the second Gen-v3 checkpoint is flown as it is, with the low-level landing finalizer. The gates use the validation starts only and their thresholds were fixed before any flight; the test is flown once after they pass and is judged by the representative thresholds.
canonical.mission: Find the blue landing pad and land on it.
canonical.band_note: A start stands at least 5 m clear of every object, the pad included, so the nearest starts are about 12 m from the pad's centre.

representative.what: every validation start; also the standard the test is read by

gen_v3c.description: Gen-v3c: a small correction of the second Gen-v3 checkpoint for one failure, target selection when an object that shares the named object's colour or shape is what the view shows (docs/gen_v3c_hard_negative_grounding.md). Nothing about the model changes: same inputs, same LoRA and head, chunk 4, FiLM and proprio off. About a hundred added episodes, a short fine-tune from generalization_v3b with half of the drawn frames from the earlier data, a pilot check of a dozen flights, and a fresh validation set behind the canonical gates. Everything here was fixed before any episode was recorded.
gen_v3c.seed_note: 10000-15999 belong to the second round of Gen-v3 additions, so the new ranges start at 20000.
gen_v3c.reach_from: two sites count as neighbours when a start inside the 44 m range of one can have the other in view: the 42 m pairs and the three longer ones (51, 57, 65 m)

hard_negative.description: What the added episodes show. `first`: the first view holds an object of the named one's colour (or shape) near its middle, and the named object is outside the view; the teacher keeps turning and goes to the named one. `lost`: the named object is in view and the approach has begun, then a forced turn (flown, never a label) puts a related object in the middle of the view and the named one outside it; the teacher keeps turning until it has the named one again. `swap`: a `first` pose flown again in the layout that exchanges the two objects, so the same view now holds the named one. `query`: a `first` pose told to go to the object in view instead. Rows are [named object, object in view]; counts are [train, val].

swap.of_note: of every eight swap twins, five are of colour poses and three of shape poses

fine_tune.description: Fixed before the run. A correction, not a retraining: the second Gen-v3 checkpoint goes on at a quarter of its learning rate (its own run ended at 2.5e-5 after decaying from 2e-4), for 2,000 updates of 4 frames. Half of the drawn frames come from the added episodes and half from everything the checkpoint was trained on, so that search, plain grounding, approach, landing and the approach-or-land pairs stay in front of it. The checkpoint kept is chosen by the same rule as before, on validation frames that are half new and half old. Among the added frames, the ones on which the choice of object is made are drawn three times as often: every frame of a hard-negative episode without the named object in view, and the first eight frames of a swap or query twin. They are about a fifth of the added frames, and without this each would be drawn about once. (This weight was added after the plan was committed and before any training; nothing had been trained or flown.)
fine_tune.validation_mix: every validation frame of the added episodes and as many frames of the earlier validation episodes, drawn in proportion to the teacher's states

pilot.description: A dozen flights in two layouts no episode was recorded in, before any flight on the fresh validation set: four with an object of the named one's colour in the first view and the named one outside it, two the same with an object of its shape, two with the named pad lost to a forced turn that leaves a related object in view, two position swaps, two with nothing related in the first view. The second Gen-v3 checkpoint flies the same twelve for reference. If the check is not passed the answer of this stage is DATA CORRECTION INSUFFICIENT; no more episodes are added.

gates.description: The canonical gates with the same numbers, on the fresh validation set (configs/gen_v3c_canonical_validation.json) read by canonical_evaluator_v2. Smoke first; the other validation starts only if it is passed; the 48 canonical test starts once, only after both are passed and the model, the finalizer, the evaluator and the configuration are fingerprinted.

smoke.what: ten validation starts: in every band a landing with the pad in view, one with it out of view and the first one's approach twin, and one landing on the red pad

representative.what: every validation start; also the standard the test is read by

validation.past_from: as in the canonical sets: the related object anywhere in the first view, within 60 m

regression.description: Has the correction cost anything it could do before? Eight starts of each earlier set, chosen by position in the file before any Gen-v3c flight, compared with what the second Gen-v3 checkpoint did on the same starts. The long-range starts are farther than 44 m and stay outside the canonical baseline.
regression.rule: a set lists its starts in cycles of objects or sentences, so the starts are taken at positions (k * step) mod n, with step the smallest number from n / count up that shares no factor with n; L takes three of each of L1, L2 and L3

grounding_architecture.description: Two architecture experiments on the Gen-v3c data as it is (docs/language_vision_grounding_architecture.md): does language condition the visual representation too weakly? Experiment 1 is FiLM on the visual features; experiment 2, a language-to-vision cross-attention adapter, is run only if FiLM does not pass, and starts from the Gen-v3c checkpoint again, not from the FiLM one. Nothing else changes: the dataset, the sampling weights, the teacher, evaluator v2, the landing finalizer, the action space, the L1 head, chunk 4, execute 1, the 44 m range. No episode is added. The 48 canonical test starts and the Depot set stay sealed. Everything here was fixed before any architecture was trained or any pilot flight flown.
grounding_architecture.dataset: generalization_v3c: the Gen-v3c merge, with its validation mix (val_mix)
grounding_architecture.layouts_note: the six layouts of each scene that no episode was recorded in; earlier evaluation sets flew in them from other starts

film.what: gamma(l) * x + beta(l) on the vision encoder's patch features, one gamma and one beta per feature channel, the same for every patch; l is the mean of the instruction's token embeddings (the language model's own embedding table, frozen) through a two-layer MLP whose last layer starts at zero, so the module is the identity at the start
film.why_here: the first of the two places the plan names. The patch features are still purely visual there, so the sentence can turn channels up or down before the projector mixes them into the language model's space; the projector stays frozen and only carries the gradient

cross_attention.what: one cross-attention layer in which the instruction's tokens are the queries and the patch features the keys and values; what each word reads from the patches is written back onto the patches it was read from, through an output projection that starts at zero, and added to the patch features as a residual
cross_attention.why: FiLM changes every patch in the same way. Choosing the blue landing pad over the blue cube needs the sentence to pick out where in the view its object is; here each word attends over the patches and only the patches it attends to are changed

training.description: The Gen-v3c correction's schedule, from the Gen-v3c checkpoint, for both experiments: 2,000 updates of 4 frames, half of the draws from the hard-negative episodes, the same weights, the same validation mix, the same rule for the checkpoint that is kept. Trained: the new module, the correction LoRA and the action head. Not trained: the vision encoder, the projector, the language model, the AeroVLA adapter. The LoRA and the head keep the correction's learning rate; the new module, which starts as the identity, gets ten times that.

pilot.description: Sixteen starts of the kind the Gen-v3c checkpoints went wrong on, each flown twice by every model: the Gen-v3c checkpoint first, as the baseline. Nine starts put a related object in the first view where it stays longest (on the side the search turns to, or straight ahead and close) with the named object outside the view; four show it elsewhere in the view; three lose the named pad to a forced turn that leaves a related object in view.
pilot.hard_zone_from: the 36 Gen-v3b and Gen-v3c flights with a related object in the first view: 8 of the 18 with it at +10 degrees or more, or within 10 degrees and 20 m, ended at a wrong object; none of the other 18 did

pass.description: An architecture passes the pilot only if every line holds. A flight is `correct` when it ends at the named object. Lines that compare with the baseline use the Gen-v3c checkpoint's two flights of the same sixteen starts.
pass.drop_from: one flight is the spread seen when the same start was flown again; a drop of one is not a difference
pass.landing_rate_of: landing missions that went to the named pad: stable physical landing, latched and disarmed

regression.what: the 33 starts of the earlier sets named in gen_v3c.regression, flown only when the lines above hold

control.description: The LoRA and the head are trained on with the module, so a pass could come from the 2,000 further updates and not from the module. If an architecture passes the pilot, the same schedule without any module is run from the Gen-v3c checkpoint and flown over the same 32 flights. The architecture is credited with the improvement only if this control does not pass the pilot as well.

selection.description: If both experiments are run, the model that goes on is chosen in this order, by rules fixed here: it must pass the pilot; then fewer flights at a wrong object; then more starts correct in both flights; then more successes; then the smaller regression; then the lower inference time and memory.

validation.description: Only for an architecture that passed the pilot (and whose control did not): 36 fresh starts with the Gen-v3c validation make-up, behind the canonical gates with the same numbers, read by canonical_evaluator_v2. The gates are judged on the first flight of every start. The starts that ask about target selection are flown a second time and reported beside the gate; that second flight judges nothing.
